reports.question: Are all atoms in this set the same schema version?
Is any decision double-counted?
How much of the situation space did this run touch, and how thin is the tail?
Which carried axes actually arrived, and which are silently empty?
Can every atom be attributed to a surface?
How often did the surface actually emit a distribution?
Which rules fired versus the residual clause? (null ruleId IS the residual)

value.conditional: P(residual clause fired | a decision was made)

reports.question: What is EV by warrant class — how much rests on rules the author labelled fear?

value.note: EV-by-warrant needs an outcome join; the warrant column is here and populated by Declared surfaces. A reconstructed audit has no per-rule warrant, hence (none declared).

reports.question: Which layer is wrong, independently of whether the recommendation was?

value.note: Empty until the surface declares a Stack (WS-324). Zero here is a COVERAGE fact, not a finding — layer probes cannot run on this set.

reports.question: What actually happened, so a prediction can be scored at all?

value.conditional: counts of the REALIZED action, over modeled nodes

reports.question: Why is coverage thin here — WHICH decisions were unscorable, and for what reason?

value.note: Atom-level, not a run-level counter. A counter says 40% were skipped; this says WHICH contexts, which is what makes "why is 4-bet coverage thin?" answerable.

reports.question: How close was this decision? Near-ties are where strategies differ.

value.conditional: top-two margin, over atoms whose surface scored 2+ alternatives

reports.question: What would rule-level ablation say, without a re-run?

value.note: Populated by Declared surfaces, whose ordered rules can lose. Zero on a reconstructed audit is a property of the surface, not a gap in the capture.

reports.question: What did we believe each opponent held here? (input to the belief-vs-truth join)

value.conditional: atoms carrying BOTH a belief and an OBSERVED truth — the only rows a calibration claim may use; hypothesized-basis rows are a category error, not noise

reports.question: What did they actually hold, and was the belief observed or hypothesized?

value.conditional: P(holding revealed | node modeled) — SHOWDOWN-SELECTED, so this subset is biased toward hands that got called down and is not a random sample of decisions

reports.question: Can this exact decision be replayed bit-for-bit?

value.conditional: P(the decision names at least one seed | atom). A decision with no seeds is replayable only if it is deterministic — which is a claim, not a default.

reports.question: Are villain decisions captured, or is this a hero-only log?
Does the table play back differently against card A vs card B?

value.note: Villain rows present means the question is REACHABLE in principle. It is NOT answerable on a recorded corpus: those villains never saw our card, so their actions cannot respond to it. A responsive Field (WS-326) is the missing half.

reports.question: Is this card affordable to run?
What did an AI-authored decision cost in tokens?
Which set is this?
Which surface produced it?
How exact can a layer ablation over this set be?

value.note: The rate is RECORDED, never inferred from how many full values are present — a low rate, a crashed run and a dropped filter are three different facts with opposite meanings. Declared vs observed disagreeing is the signal.

reports.question: Does this card earn more against a table that has been together two hours?

value.note: Without this the table-history question is permanently unanswerable — it cannot be recovered from atoms, because occupancy is a property of the table over time.

reports.question: Was the set truncated? A short read must not read as a small sample.
Which Deal Book generation does this set stand on?
